# Bridge API reference

Every member of the shared contract between the native shells and the Java bridge: the public static methods
the iOS and Android code calls by name, the JSON keys the bridges emit for the native screens to parse, and the
`-D` system properties the bridge reads at launch. It is generated from the same scan that writes
[`tools/shared-contract/baseline.txt`](../../tools/shared-contract/baseline.txt), and each description is the
Javadoc (or the comment directly above the member) in the source, so it matches the code at this commit. For
how the bridge works, which thread each call runs on, and how to change it safely, read
[bridge-api.md](bridge-api.md).

## `ConfigProfileBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/ConfigProfileBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/ConfigProfileBridge.java)

Native-UI bridge for **config profiles** — the shared-core seam the mobile shell uses to list the user's config profiles and switch the active one, mirroring the desktop `ProfilePanel`. Reads of the profile list take a `Lock` inline. A switch runs `ConfigManager#switchProfile(ConfigProfile)` on the **client thread** (via `ClientThread#invokeLater`) so its `ConfigChanged`/ fan-out — dispatched inline on the calling thread by the EventBus — mutates the engine on the engine thread; a remote-sync switch (which blocks on a network fetch) instead runs on a background executor so it never stalls a frame. Wired from `HeadlessClientUI` alongside the rest of the mobile-UI facade.

**Methods**

- `getProfilesJson()` → `String`  
  Snapshot of the config profiles as JSON:
- `init(ConfigManager cm, ProfileManager pm, ClientThread ct)` → `void`
- `isAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the native shell should offer the profiles screen (both singletons wired).
- `switchProfile(long id)` → `String`  
  Switch the active config profile by id. Returns a JSON ack immediately; the switch itself runs on the background executor and completes asynchronously (the native side re-reads `getProfilesJson()` to pick up the new active flag). The choice is saved first, so the next launch starts in it too. `ok:false` when the bridge is unwired, the id is unknown, or it is already the active profile.

**JSON keys emitted:** `active`, `available`, `error`, `id`, `internal`, `name`, `ok`, `profiles`, `sync`

## `DiagnosticsBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/DiagnosticsBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/DiagnosticsBridge.java)

The engine's half of the in-app "Share logs" report, plus a freeze watchdog that leaves a thread dump in `client.log`.

**Methods**

- `engineReport()` → `String`  
  The engine section of a "Share logs" report, as `{"names":[...],"text":"..."}`. `names` holds the logged-in character's name(s), which the shell removes from the whole report (this text included) before it is shared; `text` is plain text. Safe from any thread.
- `init(PluginManager pm, Client c)` → `void`  
  Wired from `HeadlessClientUI` once the plugin manager and client exist; starts the freeze watchdog.

**JSON keys emitted:** `names`, `text`

## `GrandExchangeBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/GrandExchangeBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/GrandExchangeBridge.java)

Native-UI data bridge for the **Grand Exchange** panel — the shared-core data feed the mobile shell uses to reflow the eight GE slots (and the saved trade history) into real native controls instead of rendering the Swing side panel as a flat image. Unlike `QuestHelperBridge`, the live offers are part of the core engine API (`Client#getGrandExchangeOffers()`), so the slot data is read with **direct typed access** and only the plugin's private trade-history config (stored per-RS-profile) is reached by reflection.

**Methods**

- `getGeJson()` → `String`
- `init(PluginManager pm, ClientThread ct)` → `void`
- `isAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the native shell should offer the native Grand Exchange screen (the GE plugin is loaded).
- `search(String query)` → `String`  
  Tradeable-item name search for the native GE **Search** tab — the desktop plugin's search box only fires on Enter (no live filtering) and we cannot fork the plugin, so the native screen drives this directly. Returns `{"results":[{"id","name","price"}]}` (price = the GE guide price), capped at `MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS`. Safe to call off the client thread: `ItemManager#search(String)` only scans the immutable price cache (no engine read). Empty/short queries and an unresolved cache both yield an empty list.
- `setUiOpen(boolean open)` → `void`  
  The native screen tells us when it is on-screen so we only pay the client-thread refresh while shown.
- `tick(Client client)` → `void`  
  Client-thread refresh (called each frame from `MobileUiBridge.tick`). Only works while the native screen is open; rebuilds the eight-slot snapshot (plus saved history) on a modest cadence.

**JSON keys emitted:** `available`, `buy`, `history`, `id`, `itemId`, `name`, `offers`, `price`, `progress`, `qty`, `results`, `slot`, `spent`, `state`, `time`, `total`

## `HeadlessLogin`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HeadlessLogin.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HeadlessLogin.java)

Gate 1c-ii / Phase-4 spike: the minimal slice of input injection needed to cross the `LOGIN_SCREEN → LOGGED_IN` boundary headless, in-process (no native touch bridge).

**Methods**

- `isEnabled()` → `boolean`
- `tick(Client client, GameState state, int loginIndex)` → `void`  
  Called once per `Hooks.draw` (only when enabled). Drives the login as a two-stage machine: while the EULA dialog is up (stage 1, optional) it synthesizes an Accept click; once the gamepack reaches the authenticated welcome screen (stage 2) it synthesizes a Play Now click. Each stage re-arms until the state advances.

**System properties read:** `runelite.headless.autologin`, `runelite.headless.autologin.cooldown`, `runelite.headless.autologin.eula`, `runelite.headless.autologin.eula.loginIndex`, `runelite.headless.autologin.eula.point`, `runelite.headless.autologin.legacy`, `runelite.headless.autologin.loginIndex`, `runelite.headless.autologin.manual`, `runelite.headless.autologin.maxAttempts`, `runelite.headless.autologin.point`, `runelite.headless.autologin.warmup`, `runelite.headless.autologin.welcomeX`, `runelite.headless.autologin.welcomeY`, `runelite.headless.autologin.world`, `runelite.headless.autologin.worldAddress`

## `HeadlessResize`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HeadlessResize.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HeadlessResize.java)

Phase-5 (W3) resizable de-risk: drive the headless gamepack `Component` to an arbitrary `WxH` after login so we can verify the CACIO CTC canvas + `MainBufferProvider` resize to that size (the one unproven step on the road to a full-screen landscape render).

**Methods**

- `cameraZoom()` → `int`  
  The camera zoom the game is drawing with, or -1 while logged out; callable from any thread. This is the big-viewport zoom (varc 74), which the game uses on any canvas over 434 px tall, so on every phone canvas. A load or a world hop keeps it. A zoom asked for but not applied yet (it waits out a load) counts as the one in use, so a host reading it back in between gets the zoom the game is about to draw with.
- `isEnabled()` → `boolean`
- `requestResize(int w, int h)` → `void`  
  Ask for the canvas to be resized to `w x h`; callable from any thread. Before the resize at login this replaces the boot size; after it, the client thread resizes again on its next draw. Only the newest request counts. Ignored unless the boot resize is enabled.
- `requestZoom(int z)` → `void`  
  Ask for the camera zoom to be set to `z`; callable from any thread. The client thread applies it the way the game's own scroll zoom does, clamped to the zoom limits, once logged in. Only the newest request counts. Ignored unless the boot resize is enabled.
- `tick(Client client, GameState state)` → `void`  
  Called once per `Hooks.draw` (only when enabled). Resizes on reaching LOGGED_IN, then on each request.

**System properties read:** `runelite.headless.resize`

## `HeadlessSeams`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HeadlessSeams.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HeadlessSeams.java)

Single dispatch point for the fork's per-frame headless seams, invoked from `Hooks`. The fork wires ~30 headless bridges + dev probes into the engine's draw cycle; keeping the whole chain here (instead of woven through `Hooks.draw`/) shrinks the upstream-merge conflict surface in `Hooks` to three one-line calls — the central friction point for tracking unmodified upstream RuneLite.

**Methods**

- `draw(Client client, Graphics graphics)` → `void`  
  Pre-composite seam: the very top of `Hooks.draw`, before the `graphics == null` guard and before overlays composite.
- `drawScene(Client client)` → `void`  
  Scene seam: the top of `Hooks.drawScene`, before the ABOVE_SCENE overlay renders.
- `postComposite(Client client, MainBufferProvider mainBufferProvider)` → `void`  
  Post-composite seam: after the ALWAYS_ON_TOP overlay + clientUI overlays composite into `mainBufferProvider`, before the `client.isGpu()` early-return.

## `HudDataBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HudDataBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HudDataBridge.java)

W3 Feature-A phase A2: the **read-only** HUD *data* snapshot the native HUD veneers consume. Whereas `MobileChromeBridge` publishes desktop HUD *geometry* (where the engine minimap/orbs/chat live, for cover-and-proxy), this publishes the *content* the native chat / minimap / orbs reproduce: chat lines (type/name/value/timestamp), orb values (HP/prayer/run/spec + poison/stamina), and minimap state (local player world position, compass angle, and nearby actor dots as tile offsets).

**Methods**

- `getSeq()` → `int`  
  Monotonic counter bumped each logged-in publish (at most every `#REFRESH_MS` ms).
- `getSnapshot()` → `String`  
  Latest read-only HUD-data snapshot as escaped JSON (native reads this each display tick).
- `isEnabled()` → `boolean`
- `tick(Client c)` → `void`

**JSON keys emitted:** `chat`, `dots`, `enabled`, `energy`, `hp`, `hpMax`, `loggedIn`, `mapAngle`, `minimap`, `name`, `npcs`, `orbs`, `plane`, `players`, `poison`, `pray`, `prayMax`, `px`, `py`, `run`, `seq`, `spec`, `specEnabled`, `stamina`, `ts`, `type`, `value`

**System properties read:** `runelite.huddata`, `runelite.huddata.dumpSnapshot`

## `HudVeneerBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HudVeneerBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/HudVeneerBridge.java)

W3 Feature-A (A3) — controls the engine chatbox so the chat-at-top look matches the OSRS Mobile reference. A desktop probe (`ChatRelocateProbe`) proved the engine's own chatbox can be `setForcedPosition`'d to the top and STILL renders there (not occluded by the 3D viewport — unlike tab stones). So instead of reproducing the chat natively, we relocate the engine's pixel-perfect chat (tabs / scrollback / colours / input all stay live, since it IS the real chat) and flip it to OSRS transparent-chat mode.

**Methods**

- `continueDialogue()` → `void`  
  Native: advance the open chat dialogue. Applied on the client thread in `tick`.
- `getChatLines()` → `String`  
  Native: the live chat MESSAGE lines (escaped JSON) for the active tab, with pre-parsed colour runs, for the native top-rendered chatbox. Read lock-free on the JNI thread; published on the client thread in `tick`, only under `-Drunelite.hudveneer.chatlines=true` (`{"loggedIn":false}` otherwise). Shape: `{"loggedIn":true,"view":N,"seq":K,"lines":[{"name":"..","type":N,"ts":N,"text":"..", "runs":[{"o":N,"l":N,"c":RGB,"u":1}]}],"input":{"name":"..","text":".."}}` — lines OLDEST-first.
- `getChatSnapshot()` → `String`  
  Native: the live chat-tab geometry/state snapshot (escaped JSON) for the enlarged native tab veneer — per-tab canvas bounds, selected/new-message state, and the live filter sub-label + colour. Read lock-free on the JNI thread; published on the client thread in `tick`.
- `getChatSnapshotSeq()` → `long`  
  Monotonic counter bumped once per CHANGED chat-tab snapshot — native skips the copy when it is unchanged.
- `getDialogueJson()` → `String`  
  Native: the open dialogue's content for the native opaque-parchment renderer, or `"{}"` when none. Shape: `{"type":"npc|player|both|message|options|levelup","name":"..","text":"..","runs":[..], "continue":true,"options":[{"text":"..","runs":[..],"digit":N}],"head":{"x":,"y":,"w":,"h":}}` — bounds are canvas px. The native side draws the parchment over the chatbox region with a cutout at `head` so the engine's real 3D head model shows through. Taps go to `continueDialogue()` / `long)`: a click on the CONTINUE widget resolves against the scene behind the chatbox and walks the player, and a synthesized SPACE comes back consumed without advancing anything. `digit` is the engine child index, so pass it through rather than renumbering the drawn rows.
- `getDialogueSeq()` → `long`  
  Monotonic counter bumped once per CHANGED dialogue snapshot — native skips the copy when it is unchanged.
- `getMapSnapshot()` → `String`  
  `{open, map:[x,y,w,h], close:[...], search:[...], zoomIn:[...], zoomOut:[...]}` (canvas px).
- `getMapSnapshotSeq()` → `long`  
  Monotonic counter bumped once per CHANGED world-map snapshot — native skips the copy when it is unchanged.
- `getOrbSnapshot()` → `String`  
  Native: the live per-orb canvas bounds for the minimap-orb touch veneer — `{"loggedIn":true, "hp":{"x":,"y":,"w":,"h":},"prayer":{..},"run":{..},"spec":{..},"store":{..},"worldmap":{..},"wiki":{..}}` (an orb key is absent when that orb is hidden — e.g. spec with no spec weapon). Read lock-free on the JNI thread; published on the client thread in `tick`. The native side enlarges the tap zone and proxies a precise click to the orb centre — orbs stay live engine widgets (hard-pinned), only the touch target grows.
- `getOrbSnapshotSeq()` → `long`  
  Monotonic counter bumped once per CHANGED orb snapshot — native skips the copy when it is unchanged.
- `getOverlayChatAvoid()` → `int[]`  
  The relocated chat's occupied canvas rect {x,y,w,h} for snap-corner avoidance — the native tab row only while collapsed, the full chat box while open — or null when the veneer isn't relocating the chat.
- `getOverlayInsets()` → `int[]`  
  Snap-corner safe-area insets {l,t,r,b} in canvas px (all 0 until native pushes them).
- `getOverlayMinimapAvoid()` → `int[]`  
  The minimap copy's canvas rect {x,y,w,h} while large portrait draws the windows' layer full width, so the top-right snap corner drops below it; null otherwise (the layer then ends left of the minimap by itself).
- `isEnabled()` → `boolean`
- `openTab(int tabIndex)` → `void`  
  Native: open the side-panel tab with the given index (0..13) by replaying that stone's op script — works even while the stones are hidden. One-shot; applied on the client thread in `tick`.
- `openWorldMap()` → `void`  
  Native: open the world map (FIX-5) by replaying the `ORB_WORLDMAP` orb's op script — a discoverable open path decoupled from the ~25px engine orb. One-shot; applied on the client thread in `tick`.
- `panWorldMap(int dxPx, int dyPx)` → `void`  
  Native: pan the open world map by a finger delta in canvas px (drag right = map content follows right).
- `preRender(Client c)` → `void`  
  Pre-render re-assert of the PEEK-SUPPRESSION hides — called from `Hooks.frame()`, the engine's BeforeRender seam: after the client tick that may have rebuilt widgets, before anything rasterizes. `tick` runs in the post-render draw callback, so an interface rebuild that reset our hidden flags (an item click's chat message re-running the chatbox script; a TOPLEVEL_REDRAW re-laying the tab stones) used to get exactly ONE rendered frame before the re-hide — the engine chat tabs/background flashing at the relocated top-left, and the desktop stone rows flashing at the bottom-right. Re-hiding here makes those widgets unpaintable instead of cleaned-up-a-frame-late. Hides only (cheap setHidden calls, idempotent); the position/size forcing stays in `tick` where it always ran.
- `relocateChat(int x, int y, boolean transparent)` → `void`  
  Native: move the engine chatbox to `(x,y)` (top-left of the screen). `x < 0` stops relocating. NOTE: the `transparent` flag is currently IGNORED — the relocated chatbox is always kept OPAQUE (its background sprites hidden, so the brown box never shows) so that engine dialogues render as the solid desktop parchment; the native veneer supplies the translucent chat look over the scene. The flag is retained in the signature for API stability.
- `relocateMinimap(int x, int y)` → `void`  
  Native: relocate the engine minimap+orbs cluster (`MAP_CONTAINER`) to canvas `(x,y)`. `x < 0` stops relocating. The cluster stays the live engine HUD — minimap clicks still walk and orb clicks still fire (A4 + A5 in one relocate; MinimapRelocateProbe confirmed render + click-to-walk).
- `relocateSidePanel(int x, int y)` → `void`  
  Native: relocate the engine side panel (`SIDE_CONTAINER`) to canvas `(x,y)`. `x < 0` stops. Same root-anchored relocate as the minimap; pulls the inventory/equipment panel inward for edge-to-edge so it doesn't clip under the notch. The panel only exists while a tab is open, so this is a no-op until then.
- `scrollChat(int deltaCanvasPx)` → `void`  
  Native: scroll the chat by `deltaCanvasPx` (positive = toward newer/bottom). Accumulated and applied on the client thread in `tick` via the chatbox scroll layer — no mouse wheel, so the camera doesn't zoom (the transparent chat overlays the viewport, where a wheel would zoom).
- `scrollMapPanel(int deltaCanvasPx)` → `void`  
  Native: scroll the open world map's KEY (legend) list — or the surface MAPLIST dropdown while it's open — by a finger delta in canvas px. Applied on the client thread in `tickWorldMap` via the engine's own `UPDATE_SCROLLBAR` script (the same path the scrollbar arrows use), so no mouse-wheel/camera side-effect.
- `selectDialogueOption(int digit, long seq)` → `void`  
  Native: pick an option in the open options dialogue. Applied on the client thread in `tick`.
- `setChatAreaWidth(int canvasPx)` → `void`  
  Native: the canvas-px width of the chat right of the shells' column. `0` gives the official 461.
- `setChatCollapsed(boolean collapsed)` → `void`  
  Native: collapse (hide) or expand the chat box. Tapping the active tab collapses; tapping any tab expands.
- `setChatHidden(boolean hidden)` → `void`  
  Native: hide the engine chatbox outright (used when the native veneer fully replaces it).
- `setChatPutAway(boolean putAway)` → `void`  
  Native: put the whole chat away, filter stones included, or bring it back (the speech-bubble stone by the door, 601's "Toggle Chatbox").
- `setChatTabRowHeight(int canvasPx)` → `void`  
  Native, and no longer read: the engine now draws the filter row itself at the official app's fixed 30 px (OFFICIAL_ROW_BOTTOM), so there is no taller native row to clear. Kept because both shells bind it.
- `setHudStrip(int visibleHeight, int windowTop, int windowBottom)` → `void`  
  Native: large portrait. The canvas runs `400` px past the bottom of the screen and only its top `visibleHeight` rows show; the chat and the minimap draw full size in the hidden rows and are copied back, scaled by `canvasWidth/765`, to the shown corners `relocateChat` and `relocateMinimap` ask for. The game's windows (bank, Grand Exchange, Settings, ...) open full width between `windowTop` and `windowBottom`. Every canvas point a shell sends and every rect the bridge publishes stays in shown coordinates. `visibleHeight <= 0` turns it off. See `HudStrip`.
- `setMinimapScale(int scalePct)` → `void`  
  Native: enlarge the engine minimap to `scalePct`% of its natural size (e.g. 130 = 30% bigger). `0` (or 100) = natural size. The globe + its chrome are re-laid each frame in `tick`; the cluster stays the live engine HUD, so click-to-walk + orb clicks keep working.
- `setOverlayKeepOut(int[] rects)` → `void`  
  Native: the shell's own controls over the game, as a flat `{x, y, w, h, ...}` list in shown canvas px. Replaces the last list; null or empty clears it. Any thread.
- `setOverlaySafeInsets(int l, int t, int r, int b)` → `void`  
  Native: the screen safe-area insets in canvas px (left, top, right, bottom).
- `setStonesHidden(boolean hidden)` → `void`  
  Native: hide (or show) all 14 engine tab stones. With the native 2-col tab grid driving tabs via `openTab`, the real stones are hidden so there is no leftover stone row / cover patch. Re-applied each frame (the engine rebuilds the toplevel on TOPLEVEL_REDRAW). `false` gives back the rows this hid. Only the Resizable - Modern layout is ever hidden; see `applyStoneRows`.
- `switchChatTab(int index)` → `void`  
  Native: switch the chat to tab `index` (0..7 into the 7 native tabs + Report) by REPLAYING that tab's op-script on the client thread — works even though the engine tab is hidden (a click wouldn't). One-shot.
- `switchToModernLayout()` → `void`  
  Native: switch the account's game client layout to Resizable - Modern, the one layout the native HUD supports, by pressing it in the game's own Settings > Display dropdown. The setting is the server's and account-wide, so it sticks on every client. One-shot; applied on the client thread in `tick`, and the outcome is logged as `[layout]`. See `GameLayoutSwitch`.
- `tabSprites()` → `String`  
  The captured tab-sprite payload (see `captureTabSprites`); `""` until ready. Read from native.
- `tapDialogue(int canvasX, int canvasY)` → `void`  
  Native: press whatever the open dialogue has under this canvas point. For the kinds that have no modelled continue or option row -- the ones `isDialogueOpen` finds by their chatbox attachment rather than by name -- the buttons are the box's OWN components, so only the box can name them: the point is matched against its live widgets on the client thread in `tick` and delivered as that widget's engine op.
- `tick(Client c)` → `void`  
  Re-apply the requested chatbox state each frame. Client thread.

**JSON keys emitted:** `Close`, `b`, `bh`, `bw`, `c`, `chatX`, `chatY`, `chatbtn`, `chatbtnNew`, `chatbtnSelected`, `close`, `complete`, `cont`, `continue`, `dialogueActive`, `digit`, `dlgH`, `dlgW`, `dlgX`, `dlgY`, `engineDialogue`, `filter`, `filterColor`, `frame`, `h`, `head`, `hp`, `icons`, `input`, `key`, `l`, `labelColor`, `lines`, `list`, `loggedIn`, `map`, `maplist`, `name`, `new`, `o`, `open`, `options`, `ox`, `oy`, `prayer`, `prompt`, `px`, `rowH`, `run`, `runs`, `search`, `searching`, `selected`, `seq`, `spec`, `sprite`, `stoneActive`, `stoneInactive`, `store`, `tabs`, `text`, `title`, `topLevelId`, `ts`, `type`, `u`, `v`, `view`, `w`, `wiki`, `window`, `windowOpen`, `worldmap`, `x`, `y`, `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`

Plus 3 keys built from a variable (not listed by name; the count is pinned in the baseline).

**System properties read:** `runelite.hover.text`, `runelite.hudveneer`, `runelite.hudveneer.chatlines`, `runelite.hudveneer.ifacedump`, `runelite.hudveneer.test`, `runelite.hudveneer.test.areaW`, `runelite.hudveneer.test.chatX`, `runelite.hudveneer.test.chatY`, `runelite.hudveneer.test.minimapScalePct`, `runelite.hudveneer.test.transparent`

## `InfoBoxBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/InfoBoxBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/InfoBoxBridge.java)

Native-UI bridge that gives the mobile shell a way to **right-click an infobox** — touch has no right mouse button, so the native shell long-presses an infobox to bring up its menu (the generic `Detach`/`Flip`/`Delete` options the `InfoBoxManager` attaches, plus any plugin-specific options an infobox adds to its own menu) and invokes one. Audit finding #20.

**Methods**

- `getInfoBoxesJson()` → `String`  
  The live infoboxes (ordered as `InfoBoxManager#getInfoBoxes()`), each with its menu-entry option texts: `{"available":true,"infoboxes":[{"index":N,"name":..,"text":..,"tooltip":..,"menu":["Detach",..]}]}`. Refreshed on tick while the native menu is open.
- `init(PluginManager pm, ClientThread ct)` → `void`
- `invokeInfoBoxMenu(int index, String option)` → `String`  
  Fire the infobox menu action the native shell selected after a long-press — the touch equivalent of clicking that right-click menu entry on desktop. Runs on the client thread; resolves the infobox by its current list index, matches the `OverlayMenuEntry` by option text, posts an `InfoBoxMenuClicked` (handled by `InfoBoxManager` and any subscribing plugin exactly as on desktop), and fires the entry callback if it carries one. Returns a JSON ack.
- `isAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the native shell can offer the infobox long-press menu (manager resolvable).
- `setUiOpen(boolean open)` → `void`  
  The native menu tells us when it is on-screen so we only pay the client-thread refresh while shown.
- `tick(Client client)` → `void`  
  Client-thread refresh (called each frame from `MobileUiBridge.tick`). Only works while the native menu is open; rebuilds the infobox snapshot on a light cadence.

**JSON keys emitted:** `available`, `error`, `index`, `infoboxes`, `menu`, `name`, `ok`, `text`, `tooltip`

## `JavaBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/JavaBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/JavaBridge.java)

Phase-4 (W3) sub-goal B: the native&lt;->Java facade for a *real interactive* client on both ports.

**Methods**

- `armSceneHold()` → `void`  
  Hooks.draw on a non-world game state → re-arm the load-in hold.
- `armTap(int shownX, int shownY)` → `void`  
  The finger LANDED at `(x,y)` — start resolving that point now, click nothing. A left tap is only posted when the finger lifts, but the engine-resolved gate it then has to pass (`tapTick`: move the synthetic cursor, wait for the engine to demonstrably resolve the point) does not have to run after the lift. Running it here spends those frames while the finger is still down, so the lift can post the click immediately (`commitArmedTap`) instead of a few frames later — which is all the "taps feel delayed" latency that is ours to remove. Safe to call for a touch that never becomes a tap: the gate only moves the pointer, which performs no action, and no button goes down before the lift, so an arm nobody commits is simply dropped by `cancelArmedTap()`, by the next tap, or by `ARMED_TIMEOUT`.
- `cameraZoom()` → `int`  
  The camera zoom the game is drawing with, or -1 while logged out (or with the canvas resize off). A host reads it to remember a zoom per screen of a foldable. Any thread. See `HeadlessResize#cameraZoom`.
- `cancelArmedTap()` → `void`  
  The touch that armed turned into something else — a camera drag, a long-press menu, a pinch — so no click is coming for it. Drop the arm. Nothing was pressed for it, so there is nothing to release. Never touches a tap that has already been committed and clicked.
- `canvasHeight()` → `int`
- `canvasWidth()` → `int`  
  Canvas dimensions for sizing the EAGL FBO (queried by the native createGLContext). 0 if no client yet.
- `clearHover()` → `void`  
  Native-facing alias for `parkPointer()` (the JNI side resolves this name; keep it stable). Called when a camera/pinch gesture begins, which is one of the moments the finger stops being a pointer.
- `devSimulateReconnect(int seconds)` → `void`  
  Developer test hook: force `HeadlessLogin#isReconnecting()` true for a few seconds so the native "Reconnecting…" overlay + snapshot path can be exercised WITHOUT dropping the real game socket. Purely a UI/plumbing test — it does not touch the connection or the reconnect budget.
- `drawSelection(Client c)` → `void`  
  Draw the selection feedback INTO the game frame (client thread, from `Hooks.draw` after the overlays composite, before the blit snapshot): a tight model outline on the just-selected entity for a beat. Tighter than a native polygon of the convex hull and it tracks the moving entity, since it's the engine's own model silhouette. (The walk destination tile is left to RuneLite's Tile Indicators plugin.)
- `getFrameHeight()` → `int`
- `getFramePixels()` → `int[]`  
  The latest *complete* composited frame as packed `0x00RRGGBB` ints (a stable snapshot, not the live back buffer; the top byte is not alpha, and both native readers draw the frame opaque). Returns `null` before the first frame.
- `getFrameSeq()` → `int`  
  Monotonically increasing counter bumped once per published frame. The native side caches the last value it rendered and skips the `CGImage` rebuild when it is unchanged (the display refreshes faster than the engine composites), so an idle login screen costs almost nothing per tick.
- `getFrameWidth()` → `int`  
  ---- Live framebuffer blit (native pulls these each screen refresh) --------------------------------
- `getGpuFrameSeq()` → `int`  
  The base-GPU liveness counter: non-zero once `gpuPublish` has read back at least one real GPU frame (counted before the display warmup gate, so the login screen counts too). The native boot crash-cookie reads this to distinguish "GPU renderer actually rendered" from mere CPU login frames (which bump `frameSeq`), so it clears the cookie only after true GPU provenance - without demoting a healthy GPU to CPU when the player quits at the login screen before the world warms up.
- `getInteractTapSeq()` → `int`  
  Monotonic counter bumped whenever a tap's CONSUMED click was an interaction (native haptic cue).
- `getInventoryBounds()` → `int[]`  
  DRAG-1: the live inventory item-grid bounds {x, y, w, h} in canvas px; w &lt;= 0 means not visible.
- `getLastTapKind()` → `int`  
  Native: the kind of the most recently resolved tap (`TAP_KIND_*`).
- `getLastWidgetBounds()` → `long`  
  Native: the last WIDGET-kind tap's canvas-px bounds packed as `x<<48 | y<<32 | w<<16 | h` (each a 16-bit field; canvas coords never exceed that). Read after `getTapKindSeq` advances.
- `getReorderPaneBounds()` → `int[]`  
  DRAG-1b: bounds of the visible drag-to-reorder panes, packed as `[x,y,w,h]` per pane in canvas px (Prayer / Spellbook / Bank, in that order, skipping any not on-screen). Empty = none visible. The native shell hit-tests a one-finger drag's start point against these to route it as an engine reorder drag (`onTouch`) rather than a camera pan.
- `getScrollableRects()` → `int[]`  
  DRAG-2: bounds of all visible, overflowing scroll-layer widgets, packed as `[x,y,w,h]` per rect in canvas px (capped at `#MAX_SCROLLABLE_RECTS`). This is the Android-safe snapshot counterpart to `isEngineScrollableAt` (an off-thread point hit-test iOS calls synchronously per touch): Android's UI thread cannot make that per-touch JNI call into HotSpot, so it hit-tests this pre-snapshotted array lock-free (published in the getSnapshot payload as `scrollRects`), mirroring how DRAG-1b's `getReorderPaneBounds` is consumed. Empty = no scrollable interface visible, or the snapshot is not armed (`-Drunelite.bridge.scrollrects`, Android only). Refreshed at most every 100 ms.
- `getTapKindSeq()` → `int`  
  Native: bumps once per resolved left tap (pair with `getLastTapKind`).
- `getTextInputKind()` → `int`  
  What kind of keyboard the open game field wants: `0` none, `1` text, `2` a number (an "Enter amount" prompt or the Grand Exchange quantity/price entry). Non-zero exactly when `isTextInputOpen()` is true. The shells show a number pad for `2`.
- `gpuFrameBackBuffer(int w, int h)` → `int[]`  
  The next back buffer (w*h ints), allocated/resized as needed, for the native shim to write into.
- `gpuPublish(int w, int h)` → `void`  
  Publish the back buffer the native shim just filled (vertical-flipped, R/B-swizzled 0x00RRGGBB).
- `heapStats()` → `String`  
  Developer diagnostics: the JVM heap as "usedMB/maxMB" (e.g. `"142/512"`). Distinct from the OS resident memory the shell reads via mach — this is the Java-heap pressure the GC actually manages.
- `invokeMenuEntry(int parentDisplayIndex, int childIndex)` → `void`  
  MENU-1: commit a right-click SUBMENU child the native menu drilled into. The engine renders submenu children in a flyout, not as rows of the main menu, so the `selectMenuPoint` click-through (which targets a main-menu row's canvas geometry) can't reach them. Instead we resolve the child in the live — and, while the right-click menu is open, *frozen* — menu tree by the same (parent display index, child index) the `MenuPeekBridge` snapshot published, then run its action directly: a RuneLite-registered `onClick` consumer (how Menu-Entry-Swapper / Ground-Items / NPC-tag submenu items are built) is invoked as the engine would, else fall back to `menuAction`. Runs on the client thread (menu reads + onClick are client-thread-only). The native side closes the now-stale engine menu separately (a title-strip click), exactly like a cancel.
- `isEnabled()` → `boolean`
- `isEngineScrollableAt(int shownX, int shownY)` → `boolean`  
  SCROLL-SPIKE: true if a scrollable engine interface widget is under the canvas point (x,y) — a visible widget whose scroll layer overflows (`getScrollHeight() > getHeight()`) and whose bounds contain the point. The native shell calls this at pan-begin to decide whether a one-finger drag should scroll an open interface (bank / GE / quest list / settings / collection log …) — emitted as wheel notches the engine routes to the hovered scrollable, exactly like the desktop mouse wheel — instead of rotating the camera. Returning false leaves the drag a camera pan, so a drag over the bare viewport never scroll-leaks into a zoom.
- `isTextInputOpen()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the gamepack currently has a text field open and awaiting input — a search box (bank/GE/world map), a private-message recipient, an "enter amount/name" dialog, etc. (`VarClientInt.INPUT_TYPE` is non-zero), or the legacy login screen's credential/authenticator entry. The native shell polls this to auto-raise the soft keyboard when the game asks for text and dismiss it when the field closes, so typing is summoned from inside the game, not a chrome button.
- `noteSceneDraw()` → `void`  
  Hooks.drawScene → count a rendered 3D frame.
- `onCameraDrag(int dxPixels, int dyPixels)` → `void`  
  Rotate the camera by a two-finger pan: apply the raw pixel delta `(dxPixels,dyPixels)` to the camera yaw/pitch *targets* directly via the client API (no synthesized middle-mouse, so it is independent of the "middle mouse moves camera" setting). Yaw wraps mod 16384 (JAU14); pitch clamps to the normal RS range. Only acts in-game. The native side sends raw pixel deltas; sensitivity + sub-pixel accumulation live here.
- `onClick(int shownX, int shownY, int button)` → `void`  
  A discrete tap at `(x,y)` (gamepack-canvas pixels): the full focus-prime + move + press + release + click sequence — the proven `HeadlessLogin.synthesizeClick` shape. `button` is 1 (left tap: walk / interact / select a menu entry) or 3 (long-press: open the right-click menu).
- `onClickPrecise(int shownX, int shownY, int button)` → `void`  
  A *precise* left/right click at exactly `(x,y)` — same proven move+click shape as `onClick`, but with **no snap-to-entity resolution**. This is for deliberate UI proxies (the native chrome tapping a tab stone / orb / widget), where the coordinate is already the exact target and touch-forgiveness must NOT redirect it: with a full-screen world viewport, snap would otherwise pull a tab-stone click onto a nearby world entity. Keeps the two-cycle move→click (so the engine re-targets the widget before the click) but feeds the literal point.
- `onKeyStroke(int vk)` → `void`  
  Press + release one non-text key by its AWT virtual-keycode (`KeyEvent.VK_*`) — backspace, enter, escape, tab, arrows, etc. Backspace/enter/tab also emit the matching `KEY_TYPED` control char (a gamepack text field deletes/submits on those). Posted from the hidden field's delete/return callbacks and any on-screen key.
- `onKeybind(int keyCode, int modifiers)` → `void`  
  KEY-1: fire a plugin's configured action-hotkey by synthesizing the exact key chord its `HotkeyListener` (or raw `KeyListener`, e.g. Bank search) listens for. `Keybind.matches` reads the event's extended key-code + extended modifiers, so a single matched `KEY_PRESSED` (with the modifier mask baked into the event — no separate modifier-key presses needed) triggers `hotkeyPressed`; the paired `KEY_RELEASED` clears the listener's pressed latch so it can fire again next time. Delivered like our other key synthesis: handed to the canvas's own `KeyListener`s on the EDT, because a posted `KeyEvent` is routed by the `KeyboardFocusManager` to the focus owner and headless there is none, so nothing posted arrives. That is NOT the same as a hardware key: it bypasses AWT's dispatch, so only listeners registered on this canvas are reached and anything AWT would do around them does not happen. It is enough for the listeners the engine and RuneLite register there. Modifier-only binds (no main key) are ignored — those are hold-to-modify, not fire-once.
- `onMiddleClick(int shownX, int shownY)` → `void`  
  Middle-button (BUTTON2) click at `(x,y)` — a discrete press+release+click, the touch equivalent of a mouse middle-click. Posts through the same canvas path as `onClick`; the engine handles it per its own "middle mouse button" setting (opens-menu / camera). No client-thread aim-assist (unlike a left/right tap) — middle-click is a deliberate, literal-point action.
- `onMove(int shownX, int shownY)` → `void`  
  Move the pointer to `(x,y)` with no button held — a plain `MOUSE_MOVED`. This is the "hover" primitive: it updates the gamepack's recorded mouse position so the open right-click menu highlights the entry under the finger as it slides. Distinct from a drag (which holds a button and posts `MOUSE_DRAGGED` via `onTouch`) so the menu-track gesture can't be confused for one.
- `onTapMove(int x, int y)` → `void`  
  One sample of an armed contact's travel, at `(x,y)` (gamepack-canvas pixels). Both shells send every sample here and nothing is posted for any of them: no button is down before the lift, and a move during the settle would push the engine's cursor off the point the gate is resolving.
- `onText(String s)` → `void`  
  Type committed text — for each character post `KEY_PRESSED` + `KEY_TYPED` + `KEY_RELEASED`. The gamepack's text fields (chat, search, username/password) consume the `KEY_TYPED` char, which carries the exact character (and case) the iOS keyboard committed. Called from the hidden `UITextField`'s change callback, so autocorrect/paste arrive as one coherent string.
- `onTouch(int type, int shownX, int shownY, int button)` → `void`  
  One phase of a drag stream — `TOUCH_DOWN`/`TOUCH_MOVE`/`TOUCH_UP` at `(x,y)`, `button` 1 or 3. DOWN presses, MOVE drags (or hovers when not pressed), UP releases — with NO synthesized click (unlike a tap, which goes through `onClick`). Both shells drive it for an item drag (the inventory and the reorder panes), where a release must not register as a click.
- `onWheel(int shownX, int shownY, int rotation)` → `void`  
  Scroll the wheel by `rotation` notches at `(x,y)` — a `MouseWheelEvent`, which `Hooks.mouseWheelMoved` routes through `mouseManager` exactly like a `MouseEvent`. Pinch-zoom maps to this: negative `rotation` = wheel up = zoom in. `(x,y)` is the pinch centroid so the gamepack zooms about it.
- `parkPointer()` → `void`  
  The finger is off the glass: post `MOUSE_EXITED` so the engine knows there is no pointer, and leave the recorded position where the finger actually left it.
- `presentReady()` → `boolean`  
  Direct-present (no gpuPublish gate): the native shell polls this to know when the world is warmed up (geometry uploaded), so it can reveal the GPU layer over the CPU loading-screen blit without a sky flash.
- `register(Client c)` → `void`  
  Called at the top of `Hooks.draw` each frame to keep the bridge pointed at the live client.
- `requestResize(int w, int h)` → `void`  
  Resize the game canvas to `w x h` mid-session, for a host window that changed shape (a foldable opened or closed), so the game shows more or less of the world instead of being stretched. Any thread; the client thread applies it on its next draw. See `HeadlessResize#requestResize`.
- `selectMenuPoint(int shownX, int shownY)` → `void`  
  Select an open right-click menu row by left-clicking its canvas point, then PARK the pointer one cycle AFTER the click so the engine doesn't leave the cursor sitting on that target. On a touchscreen there is no persistent cursor, so a stranded synthetic cursor would keep showing the selected object's action label and make the next tap re-resolve to it (the "stuck on the stairs" bug). The ordered invoke→invokeLater chain guarantees the park lands after the press/release/click, never before (which would cancel the selection). Used by the native menu's commit and cancel.
- `setAltHeld(boolean held)` → `void`  
  Sticky-Alt — same mechanism as `setShiftHeld`. Notably drives Ground Items' "hold Alt to highlight" (the plugin shows item names / its highlight while Alt is held). A native modifier toggle calls this.
- `setCameraHold(int dxPixelsPerSec, int dyPixelsPerSec)` → `void`  
  Hold the camera turning until released, as a pixel RATE in the same units `onCameraDrag` takes: `0, 0` releases. The shell sets it once on press instead of repeating a nudge, and each frame the elapsed share of that rate is fed into the drag accumulators — so this inherits the JAU14 unit space, the pitch clamp and the sub-pixel accumulation rather than restating any of them.
- `setCameraZoom(int zoom)` → `void`  
  Set the camera zoom, clamped to the game's zoom limits, as the scroll wheel would. Any thread; the client thread applies it once logged in. See `HeadlessResize#requestZoom`.
- `setClientThread(ClientThread ct)` → `void`  
  Wire the `ClientThread` used to resolve in-game taps on the game thread. Called once from `HeadlessClientUI.init`. Without it, taps fall back to the plain one-batch click.
- `setCtrlHeld(boolean held)` → `void`  
  Sticky-Ctrl — same mechanism as `setShiftHeld`, for the Ctrl-gated surface (e.g. middle-click-style Ctrl interactions, plugins that read `isKeyPressed(KC_CONTROL)`). A native modifier toggle calls this.
- `setMenuRenderSuppressed(boolean suppressed)` → `void`  
  Native control for the engine-menu raster gate (reverse JNI; see `menuRenderSuppressed`).
- `setShiftHeld(boolean held)` → `void`  
  Sticky-Shift: hold (or release) the SHIFT modifier so the engine's `client.isKeyPressed(KC_SHIFT)` path reads true without a hardware key. On touch there is no physical shift, yet a large QoL surface gates on it — Menu Entry Swapper shift-to-customize, shift deposit/withdraw/shop-quantity swaps, Ground/Object/NPC "Shift + right-click to mark", overlay SHIFT+right-click "Configure". A native sticky-"Shift" toggle calls this; the gamepack's own `Canvas` KeyListener (which feeds its pressed-key array) receives the posted event, exactly as our text injection does. `held=true` posts ONE `KEY_PRESSED VK_SHIFT` (no release); `held=false` posts the matching `KEY_RELEASED`. Transition-gated so a held toggle isn't re-posted every frame. (Proven on the live engine by `ShiftFeedSpike`: a single held press flips `isKeyPressed(KC_SHIFT)` true and a release clears it; if a long hold is ever observed to clear — e.g. on a focus change — a per-frame re-assert from `register` is the fix.) No `KEY_TYPED`: a modifier produces none.
- `snapshot(MainBufferProvider b)` → `void`  
  Called from `Hooks.draw` AFTER the overlays composite (the same point `HeadlessCapture` dumps PNGs) — i.e. when `mainBufferProvider` holds a *complete* frame. Copies it into a double buffer and publishes it for the live blit. Snapshotting here (not at the native read) is what eliminates the mid-composite flashing.
- `tapTick(Client c)` → `void`  
  Per-frame settle gate + click watchdog — called once per frame from `Hooks.draw` (client thread, after the engine tick rebuilt the menu). In `AWAIT_ENGINE`: accept once the engine's tracked cursor equals the tap point (proves the EDT folded our move) AND the left-click tail fingerprint is identical for `STABLE_NEEDED` consecutive frames (proves the engine rebuilt the menu from it) — then post the real click at the tap point. `MAX_SETTLE` frames caps the wait (fail-open: click anyway, never drop a tap). In `CLICKED`: time out back to IDLE if no truth event arrives (shouldn't happen — MenuOptionClicked fires for every left click incl. walk/Cancel).

**System properties read:** `java.io.tmpdir`, `runelite.bridge`, `runelite.bridge.scrollrects`, `runelite.gpuframedump`, `runelite.gpuframedump.dir`, `runelite.key.pacing`, `runelite.touch.armSlop`, `runelite.touch.armedTimeout`, `runelite.touch.clickTimeout`, `runelite.touch.diag`, `runelite.touch.hideClickCross`, `runelite.touch.selFlashMs`, `runelite.touch.settleMax`, `runelite.touch.settleStable`

## `LootTrackerBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/LootTrackerBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/LootTrackerBridge.java)

Native-UI data bridge for the **Loot Tracker** panel — the shared-core data feed the mobile shell uses to reflow the per-source loot logs into real native controls instead of rendering the Swing side panel as a flat image. Loot Tracker is a *core* plugin (a compile dependency of this client), so unlike `QuestHelperBridge` we would prefer direct typed access — but the data we need lives in package-private classes (`LootTrackerPanel`, `LootTrackerRecord`, `LootTrackerItem`) with no public getter, so the records are read by **reflection** into the plugin's private `panel` field and the panel's private `aggregateRecords` map. Only the plugin instance itself (`LootTrackerPlugin`, public) is located via `PluginManager#getPlugins()`, matched by class.

**Methods**

- `getLootJson()` → `String`
- `init(PluginManager pm, ClientThread ct)` → `void`
- `isAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the native shell should offer the native Loot Tracker screen (plugin present + reflectable).
- `resetAll()` → `String`  
  Clear the entire loot log — the native equivalent of the desktop panel's "Reset All" (no detailed view): empties the in-memory aggregate/session records and deletes the persisted `drops_*` config so it does not reappear on the next boot. Runs on the client thread (matches the other write-bridges); the next `tick(Client)` re-snapshots the now-empty model for the native side. Returns a JSON ack.
- `setUiOpen(boolean open)` → `void`  
  The native screen tells us when it is on-screen so we only pay the client-thread refresh while shown.
- `tick(Client client)` → `void`  
  Client-thread refresh (called each frame from `MobileUiBridge.tick`). Only works while the native screen is open; rebuilds the per-source snapshot on a slow cadence (the loot model only changes on a kill).

**JSON keys emitted:** `available`, `error`, `ge`, `ha`, `id`, `items`, `kills`, `name`, `ok`, `qty`, `sources`, `subTitle`, `totalValue`, `type`

## `MenuPeekBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/MenuPeekBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/MenuPeekBridge.java)

W3 touch-targeting: the **read-only** menu-peek surface the native press-and-peek UI polls each display tick. It is the productization of the `MenuPeek` de-risk probe (which proved the primitive GREEN on desktop): the engine rebuilds its menu every client cycle from the current pointer position, and the *last* entry of `Client#getMenuEntries()` is the top/left-click action (see `MenuOpened.getFirstEntry()` = `menuEntries[length-1]`). So while the native side streams the finger position through `JavaBridge.onMove` (a plain `MOUSE_MOVED`), this bridge reads the menu the engine computed for that point and publishes it for the native reticle/chip.

**Methods**

- `getPublishSeq()` → `long`  
  Monotonic counter bumped once per CHANGED snapshot — native skips the per-frame copy when it is unchanged.
- `getSnapshot()` → `String`  
  Latest menu-peek snapshot as escaped JSON (native reads this each display tick).
- `getTopFingerprint()` → `String`  
  Fingerprint of the current top (left-click) entry — `option|target|type|id|p0|p1|itemId` with tags stripped. The native side caches this to detect whether the top action changed between the press preview and release (release-revalidation), and the `MenuPeek` probe cross-checks it against ground truth.
- `isEnabled()` → `boolean`
- `tick(Client client)` → `void`  
  Build the menu-peek snapshot for this frame on the client thread. Reads the menu the engine computed for the current pointer position (which the native side moved via `JavaBridge.onMove`) and publishes it. Touches nothing — pure read.

**JSON keys emitted:** `active`, `count`, `deprio`, `entries`, `force`, `id`, `item`, `loggedIn`, `menuH`, `menuOpen`, `menuScrollable`, `menuW`, `menuX`, `menuY`, `mouseX`, `mouseY`, `opt`, `p0`, `p1`, `sub`, `tgt`, `type`, `wv`

**System properties read:** `runelite.menupeek`, `runelite.menupeek.maxEntries`

## `MobileChromeBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/MobileChromeBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/MobileChromeBridge.java)

W3 hybrid-chrome (Phase 6): the **read-only** geometry/state snapshot the native Jagex-Mobile chrome reads each display tick. The desktop `ToplevelOsm` (group 601) mobile layout is unreachable and would break unmodified plugins (see `AUDIT-RESULT-mobile-layout-toplevel-osm.md`); the hybrid plan keeps the desktop resizable root authoritative for the real game UI and *draws native chrome over it*. To do that the native side needs, every frame, where the desktop tab stones / side panel / minimap / orbs / chat live and which tab is active — so it can cover them with native rails, proxy taps to the live widgets, and highlight the active tab.

**Methods**

- `getSnapshot()` → `String`  
  Latest read-only chrome snapshot as escaped JSON (native reads this each display tick).
- `getSnapshotSeq()` → `long`  
  Monotonic counter bumped once per CHANGED snapshot — native skips the per-frame copy when it is unchanged.
- `isEnabled()` → `boolean`
- `noteFatalError(String code)` → `void`  
  Note an engine-fatal error code (from `RSAppletStub.onError` on mobile). Terminal: the shells surface a native card with a path forward instead of the Swing FatalErrorDialog that can't render headless. Safe from any thread; no-op when the bridge is disabled.
- `tick(Client c)` → `void`  
  Build the read-only chrome snapshot for this frame. Runs on the client thread (from `Hooks.draw`), where widget bounds and varcs are safe to read. Touches no widget.

**JSON keys emitted:** `activeTab`, `chat`, `enabled`, `fatalCode`, `fatalError`, `inv`, `loggedIn`, `loginScreen`, `mapContainer`, `minimap`, `orbs`, `reconnecting`, `reorderPanes`, `resized`, `rootKind`, `scrollRects`, `sessionExpired`, `sideContainer`, `sidePanel`, `tabs`, `topLevelId`, `viewport`

**System properties read:** `runelite.mobilechrome`

## `MobileUiBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/MobileUiBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/MobileUiBridge.java)

Phase-6 (W3): the second reverse-JNI facade — the *Java-owned* mobile-UI control plane, sibling to the hot-path `JavaBridge` (frame blit + input). Where `JavaBridge` is a thin pipe the native side drives every display tick, this is a *thick* facade: the native UIKit chrome (plugin list, config panel, chat-tap) calls a handful of coarse methods, and **this class owns the RuneLite-internal details** — most importantly *which Java thread* each mutation runs on.

**Methods**

- `boundKeybindsJson()` → `String`  
  KEY-1b (user-defined hotkey buttons): EVERY plugin `Keybind` (or `ModifierlessKeybind`) config item that is currently BOUND, as JSON `[{group,key,label,keyCode,mods,bind}]` — the user picks which to surface as on-screen buttons (rather than the hand-picked `hotkeyActionsJson` set). `label` is "&lt;Plugin>: &lt;item name>"; `keyCode`/`mods` are the AWT code + `InputEvent` masks (so the native side can fire), `bind` a human label. Read off live config; unbound items are omitted.
- `closePanel()` → `String`  
  Close the active panel (deactivate + dispose).
- `fireHotkey(String group, String key)` → `void`  
  KEY-1: fire a plugin action-hotkey by (config group, key) — reads the live `Keybind` and synthesizes its exact chord via `JavaBridge#onKeybind` (a matched `KEY_PRESSED`+`KEY_RELEASED`), which the plugin's `HotkeyListener` catches. No-op if the bind is unset.
- `flushConfig()` → `String`  
  Flush pending config to disk NOW, SYNCHRONOUSLY (`ConfigManager.sendConfig`, the dirty delta only). On desktop this happens on a 5-minute timer + a clean shutdown; on iOS/Android the app can be closed/killed without running either, so the native shell calls this at explicit checkpoints to make plugin toggles and config edits survive a relaunch. It runs `sendConfig` on the CALLING thread and returns only once the write has completed — callers that must persist before the process goes away (e.g. the Android logout path, which calls this then `exit(0)`) depend on that guarantee, so do NOT make this asynchronous (QA-P1-03). Because it does a synchronous EventBus post + a blocking fsync, callers on a UI/main thread should instead use `flushConfigQueued()` (enqueues `sendConfig` on the client thread; poll its write id if the caller needs to know the file is written).
- `flushConfigQueued()` → `String`  
  Persist the dirty config, but QUEUED on the client thread so it runs AFTER any setConfig writes enqueued just before it (sendConfig itself is immediate; ordering matters when seeding defaults then flushing). Returns a write id: once `getProcessedWriteId()` reaches it, the file is written.
- `gameSettings()` → `String`  
  The frame-rate cap and idle logout time the native Game settings screen shows, read from the FPS Control and Logout Timer plugins: `{"fpsCap":N,"idleLogoutMinutes":M}`, where fpsCap 0 means no cap. "" when the facade is off.
- `geAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the native shell should offer the native Grand Exchange screen (the GE plugin is loaded).
- `geJson()` → `String`  
  The cached 8-slot offer snapshot plus saved trade history (see `GrandExchangeBridge#getGeJson()`).
- `geSearch(String query)` → `String`  
  Live tradeable-item name search for the Search tab (see `GrandExchangeBridge#search(String)`).
- `geSetUiOpen(boolean open)` → `String`  
  The native GE screen tells the bridge when it is on-screen so the client-thread refresh only runs while shown.
- `getChatInputBounds()` → `int[]`  
  Chat-input bounds packed as `[x,y,w,h]` (game-canvas pixels), or `[0,0,0,0]` if hidden.
- `getConfig(String group, String key)` → `String`  
  Raw read of a stored config value (null if unset). Used by RLHDStarter's first-launch defaults sentinel.
- `getMobileUiSeq()` → `long`  
  Latest event sequence number. The panel stores this and polls `pollMobileUiEvents(long)` from it.
- `getPanelFrameSeq()` → `int`
- `getPanelHeight()` → `int`
- `getPanelPixels()` → `int[]`  
  The active panel's full ARGB image (PANEL_W x panelH), or empty if none.
- `getPanelText()` → `String`  
  The focused panel text field's current text (native pre-fills its hidden field).
- `getPanelWidth()` → `int`
- `getPluginConfig(String group)` → `String`  
  Full descriptor for one plugin's config `group`: per item the key, label, description, type, current value, and the typed metadata the native control needs (enum choices, int range, units, secret). Mirrors what the desktop `ConfigPanel` reflects, so the native side can render the same control set. Unknown/custom serialized types are returned with `"type":"unknown"` so the native side renders them read-only first.
- `getProcessedWriteId()` → `long`  
  Highest write id whose client-thread runnable has finished — the fire-and-forget write ack.
- `hotkeyActionsJson()` → `String`  
  KEY-1: the curated action-hotkeys with each one's *current* binding, as JSON `[{group,key,label,keyCode,mods,bind}]`. `keyCode`/`mods` are the AWT extended key-code + `InputEvent.*_DOWN_MASK` bits (so the native side can fire directly), `bind` a human label ("Ctrl + F" / "Not set"). Read off the live config so a rebind in the plugin's config is reflected.
- `hubInstall(String internalName)` → `String`  
  Install a hub plugin by internal name (config write + flush so it persists; load happens async).
- `hubManifest()` → `String`  
  Plugin-hub catalog as JSON. First call kicks off a one-time background manifest download and returns `{"status":"loading"}`; the native side polls until `status` is `ok` (or `error:*`). When ready: `{status:ok, plugins:[{internalName,displayName,author,description, version,unavailable,installed}]}` with `installed` recomputed live each call.
- `hubState()` → `String`  
  Hub install/remove progress. `hubInstall`/`hubUninstall` only register synchronously; the jar download + plugin load happen async, completing with `ExternalPluginsChanged`. The native hub screen polls this: while `refreshing` is true it shows a spinner; when `seq` bumps (refresh finished) it re-fetches `hubManifest()` to pick up the new installed set.
- `hubUninstall(String internalName)` → `String`  
  Uninstall a hub plugin by internal name.
- `init(PluginManager pm, ConfigManager cm, ClientThread ct, Client c, EventBus eb)` → `void`  
  Wire the facade to the live singletons. Called once from `HeadlessClientUI.init()` — the one component that already has `PluginManager`/`ConfigManager`/`ClientThread` injected — so this class stays a pure static JNI facade (the native side cannot hold a Guice-built instance).
- `isChatInputVisible()` → `boolean`
- `isEnabled()` → `boolean`
- `isPanelTextActive()` → `boolean`  
  True if the last `panelClick` focused an editable panel text field — native raises the keyboard.
- `listPanels()` → `String`  
  Toolbar list for the native shell: `[{index,tooltip,iconPng?}]` (panels only, Configuration excluded). `iconPng` is the nav button's icon as a base64 PNG so the native drawer can show the plugin's own icon in its title bar (the same icon RuneLite paints on the desktop sidebar toolbar).
- `listPlugins()` → `String`
- `loadAndStartPlugin(String className)` → `String`  
  Track G AG3-b — load a plugin that is NOT in the `net.runelite.client.plugins` core scan (e.g. RLHD's `rs117.hd.HdPlugin`, which ships in the staged rlhd jar on the classpath) and start it. Mirrors `PluginListPanel`'s lifecycle but adds the `PluginManager.loadPlugins(List<Class>)` step the core scan would normally do. Idempotent: if the class is already loaded it just (re-)enables it. Runs the whole load+enable+start sequence on the EDT (`loadPlugins`/`startPlugin` touch plugin state + assert it). `loadPlugins` resolves the plugin's `@PluginDependency` from the already-loaded core set.
- `loadPluginNoStart(String className)` → `String`  
  Load a plugin (if not already) WITHOUT starting it, so it appears in `listPlugins()` with an editable config but does not run. Same `pm.loadPlugins(List<Class>)` + `loadDefaultPluginConfiguration` as `loadAndStartPlugin` but with no `setPluginEnabled`/`startPlugin`. Used to surface the renderer plugins (GPU / 117HD) in the native panel even when they are not the active renderer — the native side then drives the actual activation via a launch-time preference (it can't hot-swap the iOS GL bridge/present). Idempotent.
- `nextLink()` → `String`  
  Drain the oldest pending outbound URL, or `null` if none. Native polls this.
- `nextNotification()` → `String`  
  Drain the oldest pending notification (`"title\u0001body"`), or `null` if none. Native polls this.
- `nextScreenshot()` → `String`  
  SHOT-2: the next auto-screenshot's sandbox file path (absolute), or null. The native shell drains this each frame and, when the user has enabled auto-save, copies the PNG into the Photos library.
- `notesAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  True if the Notes plugin is loaded — the native shell forks to its editable RuneLite-styled note panel.
- `notesGet()` → `String`  
  The current note text (empty string when unset). Lock-free config read.
- `notesSet(String text)` → `String`  
  Persist the edited note text on the client-thread config lane (fires ConfigChanged where subscribers expect).
- `notificationDefaults()` → `String`  
  The fully-populated default `Notification` (built from the RuneLite core notification settings, exactly like the desktop NotificationPanel seeds a freshly-enabled notification) serialized to its config JSON. The native per-notification sub-editor uses this as the base when customizing an as-yet-uninitialized notification, so override=true never leaves a field unset (NOTIF-2).
- `openPanel(int index)` → `String`  
  Open (realize + activate) the panel at the toolbar `index`; starts the repaint loop.
- `panelClick(int x, int y)` → `String`  
  Dispatch a click at panel-space (`x`,`y`) into the active panel's Swing tree (EDT). Drives buttons/checkboxes/combo arrows; a synthetic press+release+click on the deepest component at that point.
- `panelKey(int vk)` → `String`  
  Dispatch a single key (e.g. `VK_ENTER` to submit, `VK_BACK_SPACE`) to the focused panel text field (SC-4 / PANEL-1). Used for keys a whole-text mirror can't express, like Enter on a search box.
- `panelLongPress(int x, int y)` → `String`  
  A right-click (BUTTON3) at panel-space (`x`,`y`) into the active panel (SC-4 / PANEL-2 / §3.4) — drives context handlers (e.g. Loot Tracker reset). NOTE: a handler that opens a heavyweight `JPopupMenu` won't render into the panel buffer (the same limitation as combo dropdowns); direct-action handlers work.
- `panelMove(int x, int y)` → `String`  
  Park a hover (MOUSE_MOVED) at panel-space (`x`,`y`) so Swing tooltips/highlights fire (SC-4 / PANEL-2).
- `panelText(String text)` → `String`  
  Set the focused panel text field's whole text (SC-4 / PANEL-1) — the native side mirrors its hidden UITextField on each change, so a `setText` fires the field's DocumentListeners (live-filter search boxes: GE, plugin search, Hiscore, Skill-Calc, Notes). No-op if no field is focused.
- `panelWheel(int x, int y, int rotation)` → `String`  
  Inner-scroll a panel's Swing component at (`x`,`y`) by `rotation` wheel notches (SC-4 / §3.4).
- `pluginDiag(String needle)` → `String`  
  AG2 diagnostic: loaded-plugin count + any whose class name contains `needle`. For the routecgpu starter to log why the gpu plugin is/ isn't in the loaded set.
- `pollMobileUiEvents(long sinceSeq)` → `String`  
  Events with `seq > sinceSeq`, as `{seq, events:[{seq,kind,group,key}]}`. The panel diffs: any `config` event for a group it shows → re-read that group; any `plugin` event → re-read the plugin list (a toggle can disable conflicting plugins). Returns the latest `seq` so the panel advances its cursor even when no event matched.
- `publishLink(String url)` → `void`  
  Outbound-link channel. `LinkBrowser#browse` forwards every URL here (Wiki, HiScore, plugin "open page" links, etc.) because the sandbox has no system browser. The native shell drains `nextLink()` each frame and opens it in-app (SFSafariViewController / Custom Tabs). Bounded; gated.
- `publishNotification(String title, String body)` → `void`  
  Mobile notification delivery channel. `Notifier` forwards every fired (enabled, focus-passing) notification here because an app sandbox has no tray / taskbar / shell-out. The native shell drains `nextNotification()` each frame and raises a real OS notification (UNUserNotificationCenter on iOS / NotificationManager on Android). The in-canvas flash + in-chat game-message channels are unaffected (they render through the engine). Encoded `"title\u0001body"`; bounded; no-op unless the mobile UI is active so desktop dev doesn't accumulate an undrained backlog.
- `publishNotification(String title, String body, String soundType, int volume)` → `void`  
  As `String)` but carrying the `NotificationSound` type name (NATIVE/CUSTOM/OFF) and a 0-100 volume hint so the native shell can honor OFF (no sound) and the configured sound/volume instead of always playing the default beep (desktop-parity NOTIF-1). The sound/volume are appended as extra separator-delimited fields so an older shell that splits on the first separator still reads title+body.
- `registerNav(NavigationButton b)` → `void`
- `resetConfig(String group, String key)` → `String`  
  Reset one config item to its default, matching the desktop: unset it, then reapply group defaults so the item is restored to its declared default value (not merely left unset). Returns a write id to poll.
- `resetPluginConfig(String group)` → `String`  
  Reset an ENTIRE plugin's config to defaults, matching the desktop ConfigPanel "Reset" — reapply group defaults with override=true AND call `plugin.resetConfiguration()` so non-config plugin state (screen-marker boxes, ground-marker tiles, GE history) is cleared too (CFG-10). Config-only fake-plugins have no owning Plugin, so only the defaults are reapplied. Returns a write id to poll.
- `rlhdOverlaySelfTest()` → `String`  
  PROD-COMPAT-01 bring-up self-test: force-compile the 117HD `ShaderOverlay` debug shaders on the live driver so a strict-GLSL-ES typing regression surfaces in a device/CI run. The gamma-calibration, shadow-map and tiled-lighting overlays are dev-toggle-gated and never activate in a default login run, so their shaders are otherwise never compiled on-device. Each overlay's `setActive(true)` runs its `initialize() -> shader.compile()` on the client thread; a compile failure logs "Failed to compile shader:". Every overlay program also compiles the shared `overlay_vert.glsl`, so this covers all four reachable overlay shaders (overlay_frag.glsl is replaced per-stage by each subclass and never compiled). Reflective — the overlays live in the staged rlhd jar, no compile-time dependency. To avoid coupling to field names (a refactor would silently skip), the overlays are found by TYPE: every `HdPlugin` field whose type is a `ShaderOverlay` subclass. This auto-covers any future overlay. The summary logs `found=M activated=N` (grep `RLHD_OVERLAY_SELFTEST`); the CI gate asserts `M>=3` and `N==M`, so a reflection break (found=0) fails the run rather than passing a self-test that exercised nothing. Inert unless armed by `RLHDStarter`.
- `setConfig(String group, String key, String value)` → `String`  
  Write one config value (already serialized to its string form by the native control), queued onto the client thread — the desktop fires `ConfigChanged` synchronously, so this guarantees subscribers run where game-touching ones expect to be. The resulting `ConfigChanged` is the confirmation.
- `setFpsCap(int fps)` → `String`  
  Cap the frame rate through the FPS Control plugin, turning the plugin on if it is off. 0 removes the cap.
- `setIdleLogoutMinutes(int minutes)` → `String`  
  Set the idle logout time through the Logout Timer plugin, turning the plugin on if it is off. In minutes.
- `setPinned(String pluginName, boolean pinned)` → `String`  
  Pin/unpin a plugin (the desktop star) by display name. Persisted as the shared `pinnedPlugins` CSV the desktop `ConfigPanel` uses (RuneLite config group), so a pin set on either port — or on desktop — round-trips. The native list shows a star and sorts pinned-first. The read-modify-write runs on the client thread (like `setConfig`) to avoid a lost update, and returns a `writeId` the native side polls for the ack. Names are stored comma-stripped to match the desktop format.
- `setPluginEnabled(String className, boolean enabled)` → `String`  
  Enable or disable a plugin by class name — the exact `PluginListPanel` sequence (`setPluginEnabled` then `startPlugin`/`stopPlugin`), dispatched onto the EDT because start/stop assert it. The follow-on `PluginChanged` is the confirmation; re-read `listPlugins()` after it.
- `tick(Client c)` → `void`  
  Called each frame from `Hooks.draw` (the client thread) when the facade is on. Snapshots the chatbox text-entry widget bounds + visibility into volatiles so the native shell can (a) know where to hit-test a chat tap and (b) raise the soft keyboard when the field is live — without doing any widget read from the JNI thread.
- `unregisterNav(NavigationButton b)` → `void`

**JSON keys emitted:** `available`, `bind`, `group`, `key`, `keyCode`, `label`, `mods`, `ok`, `queued`, `reason`, `refreshing`, `results`, `seq`, `status`, `writeId`

**System properties read:** `runelite.mobileui`

## `OverlayBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/OverlayBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/OverlayBridge.java)

Native-UI bridge that drives an overlay **edit mode** for the mobile ports. On desktop, overlays are repositioned by Alt-dragging them around the canvas and dropping them onto snap corners; touch has no Alt-drag, so the native shell instead presents an explicit edit mode and calls into this bridge to enumerate the movable overlays, push a new preferred location / snap corner, and reset an overlay to its default.

**Methods**

- `getOverlaysJson()` → `String`  
  Snapshot of the overlays the user can reposition, as JSON:
- `init(PluginManager pm, ClientThread ct)` → `void`  
  Wired the same way as the other mobile bridges. Only the `ClientThread` is stored here; the `OverlayManager` is resolved lazily (it is not available this early). `pm` is accepted to match the bridge wiring convention even though this bridge does not need it.
- `isAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the native shell should offer overlay edit mode (the overlay manager has been resolved).
- `resetOverlay(String name)` → `String`  
  Reset `name` to its default position / size / location and persist the reset. Client thread.
- `setOverlayPreferredLocation(String name, int x, int y)` → `String`  
  Move `name` to an explicit pixel location and persist it. Setting a preferred location also implies a free (non-snapped) position, so the preferred snap position is cleared. Runs on the client thread.
- `setOverlayPreferredPosition(String name, String positionName)` → `String`  
  Snap `name` to a corner by `OverlayPosition` name (e.g. `"TOP_LEFT"`) and persist it. Snapping to a corner clears any free preferred location. Runs on the client thread.
- `setUiOpen(boolean open)` → `void`  
  The native screen tells us when it is on-screen so we only pay the client-thread refresh while shown.
- `snapPositionForPoint(int x, int y, int canvasW, int canvasH)` → `String`  
  Returns the name of the nearest snap-corner `OverlayPosition` for a dropped point, so native edit mode can show a snap preview while the finger drags. The canvas is divided into a 2x3 grid of corners (top / bottom rows x left / center / right columns); we pick the row by which half of the height the point is in, and the column by which third of the width it is in. This mirrors the five real snap corners the desktop renderer uses (TOP_LEFT / TOP_CENTER / TOP_RIGHT / BOTTOM_LEFT / BOTTOM_RIGHT); BOTTOM_CENTER is not a snap corner, so the bottom-center third also resolves to BOTTOM_LEFT to match.
- `tick(Client client)` → `void`  
  Client-thread refresh (called each frame from `MobileUiBridge.tick`). Only rebuilds while the native edit screen is open, on a slow cadence (bounds change as the user moves overlays).

**JSON keys emitted:** `available`, `bounds`, `dynamic`, `error`, `movable`, `name`, `ok`, `overlays`, `position`, `resizable`, `snappable`

## `QuestHelperBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/QuestHelperBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/QuestHelperBridge.java)

Native-UI data bridge for the **Quest Helper** hub plugin — the one panel whose dense, interactive Swing UI does not survive being rendered as a flat image on mobile, so the native shell reflows it into real UIKit controls. Quest Helper is an *external* plugin (loaded by a child class loader, not a compile dependency of this client), so every access here is **reflection**, and **every call is defensive**: if the plugin is absent, a different version, or the reflected shape has moved, we report `available:false` and the native side silently falls back to the generic rendered-panel surface.

**Methods**

- `getQuestActiveJson()` → `String`
- `getQuestListJson()` → `String`
- `init(PluginManager pm, ClientThread ct)` → `void`
- `isAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the native shell should offer the native Quest Helper screen (plugin present + reflectable).
- `setUiOpen(boolean open)` → `void`  
  The native screen tells us when it is on-screen so we only pay the client-thread refresh while shown.
- `startQuest(String questName)` → `void`  
  Start the helper for `questName` (client thread — it reads/writes live quest state).
- `stopQuest()` → `void`  
  Stop/clear the active helper (client thread).
- `tick(Client client)` → `void`  
  Client-thread refresh (called each frame from `MobileUiBridge.tick`). Only works while the native screen is open; rebuilds the (heavier) quest list on a slow cadence and the active-quest snapshot faster.

**JSON keys emitted:** `active`, `available`, `difficulty`, `general`, `items`, `name`, `quests`, `state`, `steps`, `type`

## `RLHDStarter`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/RLHDStarter.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/RLHDStarter.java)

Track G AG3-b — bring up the 117HD (RLHD) plugin (Zone renderer) on the device. Sibling of `RouteCGpuStarter`, but RLHD is NOT a built-in plugin: it lives in the staged `client-<ver>-rlhd.jar` on the classpath (package `rs117.hd.*`), OUTSIDE the `net.runelite.client.plugins` package `PluginManager.loadCorePlugins()` scans — so it is never auto-discovered. This helper, armed by `-Drunelite.routecrlhd=true` and run per `Hooks.draw` once there is a drawing canvas, loads it via the public `PluginManager.loadPlugins(List<Class>)` path (`MobileUiBridge#loadAndStartPlugin`) and starts it. `HdPlugin` declares `conflicts="GPU"`, so `startPlugin` disables the base gpu plugin automatically (do NOT also arm `RouteCGpuStarter` in this mode). `HdPlugin.startUp` defers the GL work onto the client thread and retries until `textureManager.vanillaTexturesAvailable()` and the canvas is valid — so the load is issued ONCE and we then just force the canvas valid + watch for `client.isGpu()`. Inert (mutates nothing) unless the flag is set.

**Methods**

- `isEnabled()` → `boolean`
- `tick(Client client)` → `void`  
  Per `Hooks.draw`: load + start 117HD once in-world, then force the canvas valid until it activates.

**JSON keys emitted:** `ok`

**System properties read:** `runelite.gfxIos`, `runelite.rlhdOverlaySelfTest`, `runelite.routecrlhd`

## `RuneLiteAccountBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/RuneLiteAccountBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/RuneLiteAccountBridge.java)

Native-shell bridge for the **RuneLite account** (config sync), distinct from the Jagex game login. Lets the mobile UI start/stop the runelite.net OAuth login and read the current session. `SessionManager#login()` starts a local `localhost:<port>` server, fetches the OAuth url, and hands it to the native shell through `LinkBrowser` (Custom Tab / SFSafariViewController). When the loopback redirect completes, the session opens and `ConfigManager` syncs the user's profiles + installed external plugins.

**Methods**

- `getSessionJson()` → `String`  
  `{"available":bool,"loggedIn":bool,"username":".."}` — the current session, read off-thread.
- `init(SessionManager sm)` → `void`
- `isAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the native shell should offer the RuneLite-account login (the session manager is wired).
- `logout()` → `void`  
  Sign out of the RuneLite account (closes the session server-side + deletes the saved session).
- `startLogin()` → `void`  
  Begin the RuneLite-account OAuth login. Opens the OAuth url in the native browser; completes asynchronously when the localhost redirect returns. Safe to call repeatedly.

**JSON keys emitted:** `available`, `loggedIn`, `username`

## `TimeTrackingBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/TimeTrackingBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/TimeTrackingBridge.java)

Native-UI data bridge for the **Time Tracking** core plugin — the panel whose dense grid of farming patches, bird houses, timers and stopwatches reads poorly when rendered as a flat image on mobile, so the native shell reflows it into real countdowns. Unlike `QuestHelperBridge` (an external, reflection-only plugin), Time Tracking ships *inside* this client, so we access its public model with **direct typed calls** (`FarmingTracker`, `BirdHouseTracker`, `FarmingContractManager`, `ClockManager`) and fall back to reflection only for the few package-private corners (the per-clock and per-bird-house detail). The plugin instance itself, and the trackers it `@Inject`s, are reached once by reflecting the plugin's private fields and then cached.

**Methods**

- `getTimeTrackingJson()` → `String`
- `init(PluginManager pm, ClientThread ct)` → `void`
- `isAvailable()` → `boolean`  
  Whether the native shell should offer the native Time Tracking screen (plugin present + enabled).
- `setUiOpen(boolean open)` → `void`  
  The native screen tells us when it is on-screen so we only pay the client-thread refresh while shown.
- `tick(Client client)` → `void`  
  Client-thread refresh (called each frame from `MobileUiBridge.tick`). Only works while the native screen is open; rebuilds the snapshot on a ~1s cadence (countdowns are second-resolution).

**JSON keys emitted:** `active`, `available`, `birdhouses`, `contract`, `cropState`, `durationSec`, `elapsedSec`, `farming`, `loop`, `name`, `readyTime`, `remainingSec`, `state`, `stopwatches`, `tab`, `timers`

## `UnsafePokeActivation`

Source: [`ios/dev-tools/awtsmoke/UnsafePokeActivation.java`](../../ios/dev-tools/awtsmoke/UnsafePokeActivation.java)

**Methods**

- `activate()` → `void`  
  Install CTC (toolkit + graphicsenv + SMF) on a pristine AWT state, no instrumentation. Extracted so non-probe callers (e.g. the device RuneLite boot) can activate without the AwtActivation verdict. main() = activate() + verdict, so §6.0/§6.1 behavior is unchanged.
- `main(String[] args)` → `void`

## `WorldSwitcherBridge`

Source: [`runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/WorldSwitcherBridge.java`](../../runelite-client/src/main/java/net/runelite/client/headless/WorldSwitcherBridge.java)

Native-UI data bridge for **World Switcher**. Unlike `QuestHelperBridge`, the world data is part of the client/API (`WorldService` → `World`), so reads are **direct** — no reflection.
